text-editor: **GL renderer is 4-8x slower than Cairo here.** Scrolling a 30000-line file: gl 4-8 fps, default 4-10 fps, cairo 34-35 fps; typing: gl ~5, cairo ~24. Both attempts agree (see the table).
`default` is the GL renderer (log: `Using renderer 'GskGLRenderer'`), so an out-of-the-box user gets the slow path.

The scroll input rate is the same in all modes (one wheel event per 0.25 s), and Cairo reaches 34 fps under it, so the GL path, not the input, is the limit. Text-heavy content is the case to profile (glyph/atlas upload, many small draws).
Matches the earlier synthetic result in `cases/5-performance/gtk4-renderer-matrix-gl-vs-cairo-16-scenes` (GL slower than Cairo in 14 of 16 scenes), now seen in a real app.
No GPU hang, crash or kernel message in any of the 6 runs.
loupe: **GL is ~5x faster than Cairo** for zooming a 6000x4000 JPEG with the keyboard: gl 17.7-18.2 fps, cairo 3.0-4.0 fps. This is the GPU doing what it should.
Control for the text-editor result: the GL renderer is not slow in general, it is slow for some content.
font-viewer: GL is faster than Cairo when scrolling the font list: gl 26-27 fps vs cairo 14-18 fps.
Idle phases show ~29-30 fps in every mode including Cairo: something redraws at ~30 Hz without input. Not renderer related; cause not investigated.
nautilus: Thumbnail grid and list view: GL (default/gl) and Cairo are within run-to-run noise of each other (10-21 fps, large spread between the two attempts because thumbnails load asynchronously).
No hang or crash in 6 runs; this is the 'file manager with many image thumbnails' case people use daily.
papers: PDF paging and zoom behave the same in GL and Cairo (page-down 12-15 fps, zoomed scroll ~18 fps in all modes).
The first 3 s 'idle' phase differs (default 10 fps, gl/cairo 0) because the document finishes rendering at slightly different times; not a renderer difference.
Mouse-wheel scrolling did not reach the window in the page-fit view with our synthetic input; keyboard (space) is used instead.
maps: Works under every renderer; frame rates are low (1-3 fps) because the view is mostly static and tiles arrive over the network. The phases are too static to say anything about throughput.
No hang, crash or llvmpipe. Treat this as a does-it-render check (screenshots show the world map, then the globe/country view).
epiphany: **Does not load any page on this board**: the tab stays on 'Blank page' with the load bar near the start, for the CSS/canvas/WebGL page, for a one-line local HTML file and for https://example.org. Same in default, gl and cairo.

Diagnostics kept in `diagnostics/` (screenshots): disabling WebKit's DMABUF renderer and its compositing mode, and setting the session bus explicitly, change nothing; there are no Mesa/EGL errors and no kernel events.
Cause is not isolated, so this is not a Mesa finding. It needs a WebKitGTK-side check (web process start-up on this image). WebKit's security sandbox was deliberately not disabled.
Consequence: WebGL through WebKitGTK is **untested** here. WebGL on this Mesa is covered by the Chromium/Firefox cases.
calculator: Widgets and popover only. Same behaviour in all renderers, no events. ~28-29 fps while 'idle' in every mode (see font-viewer note).
characters: Emoji category switching renders at ~22-23 fps in all three modes; search ~25 fps. No differences between renderers.
Mouse-wheel scrolling did not reach the window with our synthetic input, so categories are switched by taps instead.
clocks: Tab switch and stopwatch: same in all renderers, no events. Mostly static UI, so frame rates are low by nature.
localsend: Renders and animates (radar animation 28-30 fps) with `GDK_GL=gles`; no GPU events in 4 runs.

**Without `GDK_GL=gles` the app logs `Failed to create OpenGL context: Unable to create a GL context` and silently falls back to software rendering**, at the same ~28-31 fps. So the fps of this app says nothing about GPU speed: a CPU-rendered UI is just as fast at this complexity. Do not read the `default` columns as GPU results.
Package: Flathub aarch64 build 1.18.2, bundle copied to the board and run against the board's Mesa (not the Flatpak runtime).
ente-auth: Renders with `GDK_GL=gles` (carousel, Log in page, text field). Frame rates are low (4-6 fps) because the screens are mostly static.

**Without `GDK_GL=gles` the window stays empty** (0 frames): this newer engine has no software fallback after `Failed to create OpenGL context`. Every Flutter app on the image needs `GDK_GL=gles` set for the session.
Built from source (4.4.27) on the laptop because only x86_64 packages exist; see `../README.md`.
ricochlime: Real Flame-engine game: menu, start game and shooting taps run at 36-38 fps with `GDK_GL=gles` for 4 runs, no hangs or errors.

Without `GDK_GL=gles` it falls back to software rendering (logged) and still reaches 34-35 fps, so on this 2D pixel-art game the GPU path is only ~7% faster than the CPU fallback. Possible that the frame rate is capped by the game loop; not investigated.
firmware-updater: Impeller GLES starts and the window draws a spinner, then the app waits for the fwupd service, which is not running on this board, and stops repainting (0 fps). It never reaches its real UI, so this is a start-up check only, not a performance case.
A `snapctl` shim (prints `mode: run`) is needed because the app is snap-packaged; it lives in `~/flutter-apps/shims` on the board. No GPU events.
